A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same BaseCal research work. All 16 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices A.1–A.5, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original calibration experiments, cross-dataset evaluations, architecture and loss comparisons, and selective-classification results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Table 1 and supplementary analyses in Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 retain the same BaseCal-ReEval and BaseCal-Proj procedures, including hidden-state pairing, linear projection with MSE, frozen language models, and confidence estimation through the base model's output layer.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TriviaQA, NQ, WebQ, SQuAD, and MMLU, with the same additional test scenarios. Table 1's caption changes from four datasets to five, correcting its description of coverage already present in v1.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain Vanilla, P(True), Verbalization, Semantic Entropy, DACA on MMLU, and supervised Temperature Scaling. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the supplementary evaluations.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A.1–A.3 retain the same splits, sample counts, model configurations, ECE and Brier Score metrics, judging procedure, and cross-dataset and selective-classification protocols.

E4.justification: The hidden-state visualization, projection-architecture and loss comparisons, cross-dataset generalization analyses, and model-scale and post-training comparisons are unchanged, including Appendix A.4.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither adds repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, run-to-run error bars, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 1 retains Qwen2.5 MMLU ECE values of 0.0393 for BaseCal-ReEval and 0.0703 for DACA; the appendix loss results and generalization heatmaps also match.

T1.justification: The calibration definitions, confidence formulas, projection objective, and alternative loss equations in Appendix A.4.1 retain the same mathematical content. No assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about base-model calibration and unsupervised, plug-and-play calibration without changing generation. The claimed average ECE reductions also remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning recoverable hidden-state calibration and generalization remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning theoretical understanding, specialized architectures, and access to internal model parameters.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, early stopping, generation and judging prompts, baseline settings, and data-use details are unchanged. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the distinction between BaseCal's hidden-state approach and DACA's probability scaling and multiple-choice restriction.

P1.justification: v3 removes the Meituan affiliation and associated author markers, adds an explicit corresponding-author footnote for Fei Sun, and makes a small caption wording correction. Scientific prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1's caption changes from 'four datasets and three PoLLMs' to '5 datasets and 3 PoLLMs.' The first-page edits cause limited early-page reflow. Figures and table structures remain unchanged; pages 7–16 render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 removes a small inconsistency in Table 1's caption and updates author information. Both versions already contain the same five-dataset evidence, methods, analyses, reproducibility details, and limitations. These limited editorial corrections and layout shifts do not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
